scope: Alpha backend and play-type arithmetic; no deployment or production success claimed by this local evidence.

features.SCRUM-695: Usage versus efficiency relative to the same league play type
features.SCRUM-696: Opponent defensive weak spots ranked by allowed PPP above the same league play type

SCRUM-701.before: Regular season and playoffs were combined; duplicate player rows and missing phase were accepted.
SCRUM-701.after: Regular-season ID and season must agree; duplicate player/team/play-type rows are rejected.

SCRUM-702.before: PPP, FG% and eFG% were all averaged with possession weights.
SCRUM-702.after: PPP uses total points/possessions; FG% uses total makes/attempts; rounded source eFG% is weighted by attempts. League rates use the same denominators. The separate lagged-forecast eFG aggregator is corrected too.

SCRUM-703.before: A weaker defense reduced both baseline and context matchup scores.
SCRUM-703.after: Offense is blended directly with opponent PPP allowed; raising allowed PPP cannot lower the unadjusted score when other inputs are fixed.

formulas.efg_pct: sum(source_EFG_PCT*FGA)/sum(FGA); approximate because source rates are rounded and 3PM is absent
formulas.league_ppp: sum(league points for play type and side)/sum(league possessions for play type and side)

limits: Regular-season source snapshot only; this audit does not prove the upstream snapshot is complete.
The source has eleven offensive and seven defensive categories; unavailable defensive categories are listed, never treated as zero.
GP is a legacy sum of player appearances, not team games; new charts use possessions.
Sample cutoff is a display rule, not a confidence interval. Low-sample rows remain visible and cannot receive a Top3 weak-spot highlight.
More usage and higher historical efficiency do not establish that running a play more would cause improvement.
Score, free-throw, shooting-foul and and-one rates overlap; future outcome views must show separate rates, not a100%stack.
League statistics are possession-weighted within season, phase, side and play type, not averaged across players/teams/sides indiscriminately.
Baseline/regular ML diagnostics use observed-season features. Lagged forecast evidence is separate; prior submitted evidence is retained unchanged.
compatibility: Existing endpoint names and recommendation role checks remain.
Existing baseline/context numbers change because source scope and arithmetic are corrected.
Captured POST report snapshots preserve their supplied history; regenerated GET reports identify regular-season scope.
Saved play-type prediction and analysis-cache versions are checked against the loaded source and aggregation.
No shot data/model artifacts, teammate Request Log implementation or QuickCall rules were changed.

primary_references.supports: PPP denominator and overlapping scoring/free-throw/foul/and-one rates.
Provider fields, player/team selection and explicit season_type input.

tests.local_identity: Controlled JWT/role fixtures; live auth and browser verification are separate.
